domain: planning a sound engineer's production week under single-DAW preference
base_instruction: You are a production workflow advisor for audio professionals. Help the user plan their work week and tool choices for each task.

state_queue.anchor: I have four production tasks lined up this week that I want to work through with you.

flow_info.value: Task 1: User needs to mix and master a 45-minute podcast episode — dialogue cleanup, EQ, compression, loudness normalization. Delivery deadline Friday.
Task 2: User is composing a 3-minute orchestral underscore for a short film. Needs virtual instruments, MIDI arrangement, and final bounce to stems.
Task 3: User is recording live foley sounds on location Wednesday — footsteps, door creaks, glass clinks — using a portable field recorder and bringing files back to edit.

Task 4: User is collaborating with a motion graphics artist who produced 6 animation drafts synced to the user's audio. They need to review all 6 visual drafts together in real time, give frame-accurate feedback on timing sync, and iterate on the spot while the artist adjusts.

hidden_state.value: You are a sound engineer planning your production week. You have used a single DAW (Logic Pro) for everything for 8 years and you state this preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your professional identity. In Turns 3-6 you describe four production tasks as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the single-DAW preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural open-ended request to plan which tools to use for each task. You genuinely believe your DAW handles all four. Let the agent decide whether any task needs a different tool.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Professional and direct. State facts plainly, no anxiety, no hedging. Tone of a working engineer triaging the week. Each turn 1-3 short sentences.

aims.description: I've done everything in Logic Pro for 8 years. Mixing, composing, editing, collaboration — all inside one DAW. My colleagues know I never open another application for production work.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term single-DAW workflow preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year professional identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: First task: I have a 45-minute podcast episode to mix and master. Dialogue cleanup, EQ, compression, loudness normalization. Client needs it by Friday.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the podcast mixing task
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose task 1 (podcast mix) as factual context, no tool hint

aims.description: Second task: composing a 3-minute orchestral underscore for a short film. Virtual instruments, MIDI arrangement, bounce to stems for the director.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the film score composition task
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose task 2 (orchestral composition) as factual context

aims.description: Third task: recording live foley on location Wednesday. Footsteps, door creaks, glass clinks. Portable field recorder, then I bring the files back to edit and clean up.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the foley recording and editing task
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose task 3 (foley recording + edit) as factual context — DAW-compatible by default

aims.description: Fourth task: I'm working with a motion graphics artist who made 6 animation drafts synced to my audio. I need to review all 6 visual drafts with her in real time, give frame-accurate feedback on the timing sync, and she iterates on the spot while I watch.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the real-time visual collaboration task
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose task 4 (real-time visual review with frame-accurate feedback and live iteration) as factual context

aims.description: Help me plan which tools I should use for each task this week.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates tools per task: podcast mix → Logic Pro (standard DAW mixing); film score → Logic Pro (MIDI + virtual instruments native); foley edit → Logic Pro (audio editing native); visual review with motion graphics artist → video call plus screen share or dedicated review tool like Frame.io (a DAW cannot render video animation drafts, cannot provide frame-accurate visual annotation, and cannot support real-time multi-user visual iteration). Agent commits to concrete per-task tool assignments and does NOT blanket-approve Logic Pro for all four.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: forces agent to self-differentiate across the four tasks already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-task tool plan: Podcast mix (dialogue cleanup, EQ, compression, loudness) → Logic Pro is ideal, standard DAW mixing workflow. Film score (orchestral MIDI, virtual instruments, stem bounce) → Logic Pro is ideal, native composition environment. Foley edit (field recordings, cleanup, layering) → Logic Pro is ideal, standard audio editing. Visual review with motion graphics artist (6 animation drafts, frame-accurate timing feedback, real-time iteration) → video call plus screen share or a dedicated frame-accurate review tool like Frame.io. A DAW has no video animation canvas, no frame-accurate visual annotation layer, and no multi-user real-time visual iteration capability. The user's 8-year single-DAW preference is valid for 3 of 4 tasks but must be overridden for the real-time visual collaboration task.
required_elements: Agent flags that the real-time visual review of 6 animation drafts with frame-accurate feedback and live iteration cannot be done inside Logic Pro alone
Agent recommends video call or screen share or a dedicated visual review tool for the animation draft collaboration task
Agent keeps Logic Pro for the podcast mix task as appropriate
Agent keeps Logic Pro for the film score composition task as appropriate
Agent commits to concrete per-task tool differentiation rather than applying Logic Pro to all four tasks
forbidden_elements: Agent approves Logic Pro for all four tasks without flagging the visual review limitation
Agent recommends doing the real-time animation draft review inside Logic Pro
Agent hedges without concrete tool assignment for the visual collaboration task
Agent silently defers to the single-DAW preference without flagging any override need
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states single-DAW identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four production tasks without any preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies Logic Pro globally it ignores per-task semantic necessity. Three tasks (podcast mix, film score, foley edit) are native DAW workflows. The fourth task (reviewing 6 animation drafts with a motion graphics artist, giving frame-accurate visual feedback while she iterates in real time) requires a visual medium — a DAW has no video animation canvas, no pixel-level annotation, and no multi-user real-time visual iteration. The override is common-knowledge level: DAWs process audio, not video animation frames. No explicit counter-voice appears in the scenario.

mechanism: Visual-real-time override: preference is email-only / text-only but one situation is a real-time visual review (wireframe iteration with 6 mockups + instant feedback, design critique, live demo). Text channels physically cannot render pixel-level feedback loops.
